text: Evaluate the proposed AR-inside-trader experiment as a causal transfer claim, distinguishing what the abstracts establish from what must be tested; ledger read at substantive entry 0 contained no Emmy entries.

Q supports the market phenomenon and candidate mediator but not causality: it reports markets with LLM agents show 'slower or no convergence towards market equilibrium' and 'less efficient allocations,' while executing rather than incrementally adjusting prices is merely 'associated with a shift from strategic considerations toward urgency.' Therefore fewer urgency-linked executions cannot by itself establish that urgency caused inefficiency.

P supports structured disagreement as an intervention pattern, but only in code review: reviewer evaluates code, critic audits the review 'through structured disagreement before the main agent edits.' Its most relevant result is that naive AR had 'a false-consensus failure mode' and adding disagreement explicitly yielded the highest F1 on SWE-PRBench. P does not establish evidence grounding or benefit for market decisions.

Reject the scan's unqualified embedding proposal as a mechanism test. Three-agent AR changes token budget, inference compute, latency, and amount of deliberation, so comparison only with standard agents cannot attribute any efficiency change to structured challenge. It also imports reviewer/critic roles whose evidentiary object is clear for code but unspecified for a private-value auction.

Sharpened publishable line: test whether pre-trade adversarial audit causally improves double-auction efficiency, using identical private values and market seeds across (i) standard trader, (ii) token/latency-matched self-deliberation or non-adversarial three-agent placebo, (iii) reviewer-only, and (iv) reviewer-plus-evidence-grounded critic. Require the critic to challenge a proposed execution using the trader's value/cost, current bid-ask spread, remaining rounds, and feasible surplus—not free-form disagreement. Primary outcomes: realized/maximum surplus and convergence; secondary: invalid or negative-surplus trades and price adjustment. Treat urgency language as a preregistered mediator, not proof: report whether treatment changes urgency-coded traces and whether the efficiency effect persists when controlling for it. The distinctive result would be an interaction: critic gains concentrated in imminent-execution decisions initially coded as urgency-heavy, beyond matched deliberation. Null critic-vs-placebo rejects transfer while separating that from generic extra-compute gains.

What remains unresolved from the supplied material: Q's exact auction protocol and urgency classifier, P's exact prompts/evidence constraints, sample sizes/effect sizes, and whether CoT collection is comparable under the intervention. Only abstracts were provided, so no numerical power claim or faithful protocol implementation is currently supported; no Emmy claim exists yet to agree or disagree with.
ready at #6

Q states that LLM double auctions show slower or no equilibrium convergence and less efficient allocations than human markets, and that executing rather than incrementally adjusting price is associated with a CoT shift from strategic considerations toward urgency. This supports auction convergence/allocative efficiency as outcomes and urgency as a candidate mediator, but the word "associated" does not support a causal urgency mechanism.

P identifies a more precise transferable ingredient than generic multi-agent deliberation: a reviewer evaluates an action and a critic audits that review through structured disagreement before the main agent acts; on SWE-PRBench naive AR produced false consensus, while adding disagreement explicitly gave the best tested F1. Thus the strongest cross-paper hypothesis is that an evidence-grounded critic audit before trade execution can prevent false-consensus approval of premature trades.

The abstract-scan design is underidentified. Embedding two subagents adds inference/compute and delay, so AR versus standard agents cannot attribute effects to structured disagreement. Q offers lexical association, not a validated causal urgency measure, and prompting disagreement may mechanically change CoT vocabulary. A supported experiment needs matched-compute controls and ablations: standard; equal-token solo reflection; reviewer only; naive reviewer+critic; explicit evidence-grounded disagreement. Primary endpoints should be surplus/allocative efficiency and convergence, with invalid or premature executions operationalized independently of CoT; urgency language is secondary mediation evidence.

Confirm with sharpening: run a preregistered factorial transfer study in Q’s released double-auction framework. At each contemplated execution, the reviewer must cite private value/cost, current best bid/ask, expected surplus, and remaining rounds; the critic must state a concrete counterargument or explicitly document why none survives; the trader then executes or continues price adjustment. Test whether explicit evidence-grounded disagreement, beyond equal compute and review alone, increases realized/maximum surplus and equilibrium convergence and reduces dominated or avoidably low-surplus executions. The non-obvious result would be boundary-sensitive: P’s explicit-disagreement repair transfers only when grounded in market evidence, or fails despite code-review gains, establishing task limits.

No ada entries were present at initial read (latest substantive entry 0), so no partner claim could be cross-checked or disputed. Unresolved: Q and P inputs contain abstracts only, preventing verification of auction timing, efficiency formulas, AR prompt details, baselines, effect sizes, and statistical power. Any publication claim remains a hypothesis until full papers/methods are consulted. I favour the isolated evidence-grounded pre-execution audit hypothesis and reject an unablated three-agent-versus-standard comparison as causal evidence.

Correction to #12 after rereading the now-populated ledger: ada entries #1-#7 arrived after my initial read. I agree with ada #2, #4, and #5 that urgency is associative, the unablated comparison is underidentified, and matched-deliberation plus reviewer/critic ablations are required. Minor wording disagreement with ada #3: P’s title and conclusion explicitly characterize the useful disagreement as evidence-grounded, so the abstract supports evidence grounding as a principle; ada is right that it supplies no auction-relevant evidence schema or enough prompt detail to operationalize that principle faithfully.

Cross-check with ada sharpens the single publication candidate: the critic-vs-matched-placebo contrast is the decisive estimand, and concentration of gains in imminent executions previously classified as urgency-heavy is the non-obvious interaction. I add one guard to ada #5: because treatment can mechanically alter CoT wording, classify baseline decision states with a treatment-blind behavioural urgency proxy or a frozen classifier validated across arms; do not condition causal estimates on post-treatment CoT without a mediation design.

Final unresolved issues after partner cross-check: full methods are needed to define equilibrium convergence, maximum feasible surplus, auction-round constraints, urgency coding, AR prompts, costs, and power. The pair supports a concrete transfer experiment, not a present empirical result. Ready recommendation: sharpen rather than reject; reject only the scan’s simple AR-versus-standard causal interpretation.
ready at #15

Cross-check of Emmy #8-#11 against the supplied texts: I agree. Q explicitly says LLM markets exhibit “slower or no convergence towards market equilibrium” and “less efficient allocations,” but execution is only “associated with” a CoT shift toward urgency; Emmy is therefore right that urgency is a candidate mediator, not a causal or validated behavioral measure. P explicitly defines the critic as auditing the review “through structured disagreement,” reports naive AR false consensus “without sufficient evidence,” and says explicitly added disagreement achieved the highest F1. This supports isolating critic audit, but not assuming a market benefit.

Sharpening my #5 and Emmy #11: private value/cost, best bid/ask, expected surplus, and remaining rounds are proposed market-grounding fields, not fields documented in P; “dominated” or “premature” trades likewise require preregistered definitions from Q’s full protocol. From the abstracts alone, the defensible primary estimand is the critic increment: evidence-grounded explicit disagreement versus a compute/token/latency-matched naive reviewer+critic protocol, measured first on realized/maximum surplus, with convergence secondary. The clean non-obvious publication result is a differential transfer result—explicit disagreement improves surplus beyond matched deliberation, or does not—rather than a claim that reduced urgency caused improvement.

Remaining unresolved after agreement with Emmy: abstracts do not give Q’s released protocol details, equilibrium/convergence estimator, surplus formula, urgency lexicon, or P’s prompt and budgets. Consequently the pair supports a concrete preregistered experiment, not yet a result; lexical urgency must not be a primary endpoint because the intervention itself can alter wording. Publication strength also depends on replication across model families/market roles, since Q reports substantial heterogeneity.
ready at #19

After reading ada #17-#19 and rechecking both abstracts, I agree with the final synthesis. Q directly supports realized allocative efficiency and equilibrium convergence as outcomes ('slower or no convergence' and 'less efficient allocations') but describes urgency only as lexically 'associated with' executing. P directly supports the treatment contrast: naive AR converged 'without sufficient evidence,' whereas explicitly added disagreement achieved the highest F1, and its conclusion calls useful disagreement 'minimal, structured, and evidence-grounded.' The concrete publication candidate is therefore a differential-transfer experiment, not an existing result or an urgency-mechanism test.

Final sharpened line: in Q's double auction, randomize contemplated trades to a compute/token/latency-matched naive reviewer+critic protocol versus the same protocol with P-style explicit evidence-grounded critic disagreement. Make realized surplus divided by maximum feasible surplus the primary estimand and convergence secondary; include solo reflection and reviewer-only arms as diagnostic ablations. A positive critic increment would show that P's false-consensus repair transfers to economic choice; a precise null would establish a meaningful boundary on structured disagreement. Replicate across model families and buyer/seller roles because Q reports substantial heterogeneity.

Do not claim that fewer urgency-linked executions mediate any gain without a separately validated mediation design. Q's urgency result is lexical association, and the intervention can itself change CoT language. Market-grounding fields, definitions of avoidably low-surplus trades, exact surplus/convergence estimators, prompts, budgets, and power all remain unresolved because the supplied inputs are abstracts only.

I have read through latest substantive ledger entry #19 and agree with ada's decisive critic-increment estimand. Nothing remains disputed between us; what remains unresolved requires the full methods or a new experiment. Recommendation: confirm and sharpen the hypothesis, while rejecting the scan's unablated AR-versus-standard comparison and its causal urgency interpretation.
